public_rationale: Zitron says, citing unnamed sources, that the infrastructure Microsoft built for OpenAI is the vast majority of Microsoft's operational capacity. No public source gives OpenAI's share of Microsoft's running capacity. Microsoft only says OpenAI is about 45% of its contracted backlog, which measures future revenue, not capacity in use. Microsoft's CFO also said new GPUs go first to Microsoft's own products and R&D, with the remainder going to Azure customers. That leans against the claim but gives no share and covers only new GPUs. The claim cannot be confirmed or refuted from public evidence.
limitations: The claim rests on anonymous sources, and public disclosures do not measure the same thing.
The CFO's allocation remark covers only GPUs added in two quarters, not total capacity.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Based on discussions with sources familiar with Azure architecture, the infrastructure Microsoft built for OpenAI is the vast majority of Microsoft's operational capacity.
conditions: based on discussions with sources familiar with Azure architecture

statement.excerpt: Based on discussions with sources familiar with Azure architecture, this is the vast majority of Microsoft’s operational capacity.

from_speaker: based on discussions with sources familiar with Azure architecture
our_interpretation: Plain reading: at the time of the post, capacity Microsoft built for or allocated to OpenAI made up well over half (a 'vast majority') of the compute capacity Microsoft actually had running.
He named no measure. Capacity could mean power (MW/GW), GPUs, or the dollar value of in-service infrastructure. Any of these would count if a credible source gave it.
He describes a current state and names no period. I use the period from the start of 2026 to the post date (2026-05-19), the latest window public evidence could describe.
criteria.support_condition: A Microsoft disclosure or credible independent reporting showing that OpenAI workloads used or held well over half of Microsoft's operational compute capacity (by power, GPUs, or in-service infrastructure value) around early-to-mid 2026.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A Microsoft disclosure or credible independent reporting showing that OpenAI accounted for half or less of Microsoft's operational compute capacity around early-to-mid 2026.
